So I've taken suggestions and ideas from the various community discussions we've had, mostly from the discussions about moderation and moderators, and put together a draft for a moderation policy for our subverse. I have a tendency to write too much, so I worry that it is too long and maybe overly complicated - but I wanted to be thorough.

My goals with this are for us to have something that will serve as the backbone for ANY moderation team that exists, so that there is a continuity of experience for the community even if there are completely different faces running the show. Also just to make sure that we have a focused mod team that is all on the same page, rather than operating under different personal moderation policies.

Some of the stuff in this is common sense, so it might seem silly or redundant. Maybe it is. I think it's still good to have it penned down. I know that this could be improved considerably, which is why I think having an open invitation for the community to propose changes is important.

Anyway, I want to hear primarily from the /v/conspiracy moderators what you think about this draft, but anyone else is welcome to comment. I'm figuring that after this is in a state that the mod team is comfortable with, we'll bring it to the community for formal approval.

Here it is: https://github.com/Mumberthrax/VoatConspiracy/blob/master/ModerationPolicy.md
It all looks good to me, nothing crazy. I do like the idea of a vote for new moderators. That way the community feels involved and not like something crazy is going on behind closed doors.

yeah I agree - though a popular vote still means that there is a possibility of bad people getting a spot on the mod team. Elections would probably become politicized, and I think we at /v/conspiracy probably know better than most that popular consensus does always make the smartest decisions (arguably the voting mechanism plays a role here, but still...) - like agent K said, "A person is smart. People are dumb, panicky, dangerous animals, and you know it."

I suppose whatever method we use to add moderators is going to be susceptible to manipulation, runs a risk of malicious people getting the ability to remove posts/comments. Probably just means that there needs to be a strong focus on accountability/transparency, and good methods to remove people not acting in good faith.

Well written.

I wonder though, should there be only one "top" moderator with level 1 clearance?

Since Atko is already "top dog" it seems the next layer down should have 2 or 3, if that makes sense.

This is something that I've kind of grappled with as well. Voat currently is set up so that one person can be the "level 1" moderator of a subverse, and any other mods are always "level 2" (I use these terms because that's what they're called on the page where mods can be added/removed). The main functional differences are that the level 1 can add/remove mods, and update several more subverse settings. I don't really know how this could be changed on our end, only through some sort of site wide change.

What I think might be cool is if we had a small group of "head" moderators, sort of in an administrative or executive role. Their composition would be governed by that unnamed mechanism in the draft. then other mods could participate in executive decision making, but they'd only really be expected to handle basic stuff like removing rule breaking things. Problem with this is that it probably opens the door to oligarchy.

But yeah, right now the way Voat is set up, only one mod can have the "level 1" permissions.

I think that's a good idea as this place grows. I understand not wanting too many chefs in the kitchen, especially when a higher level mod can go rogue and make changes without consulting the others (not that they can't be changed back though)
